`tidycreel` has been accepted and is now available on
[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=tidycreel). The release is **8.0.0**.
I am pleased to see it reach this point, and grateful to everyone who has
offered questions, corrections, and feedback along the way.

If you are new to the package, creel surveys combine angler counts and
interviews to estimate fishing effort, catch, and harvest. `tidycreel` provides
a tidy R workflow for survey design, data validation, estimation, and reporting,
with the `survey` package supplying the design-based foundation.

## Install tidycreel

You can now install the CRAN release using the usual R command:

```r
install.packages("tidycreel")
library(tidycreel)
```

As of October 15, the 8.0.0 source package and binaries for Windows and macOS
are available on CRAN. The macOS binaries support both Apple Silicon and Intel
Macs. Use the command above to install the release.

To install the source release explicitly:

```r
install.packages("tidycreel", type = "source")
```

`tidycreel` itself has no compiled code. Dependencies installed from source
may require build tools.

For the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/chrischizinski/tidycreel),
use `pak`:

```r
install.packages("pak")  # Once, if pak is not already installed
pak::pak("chrischizinski/tidycreel")
```

Use the CRAN release for most analyses. Install from GitHub if you want to try
the latest development changes.

**Aerial surveys:** Use the GitHub development version for catch, harvest, and
release totals until 8.0.1 reaches CRAN. It fixes an underestimation issue in
8.0.0; non-aerial designs are unaffected
([release notes](https://github.com/chrischizinski/tidycreel/releases/tag/v8.0.0)).

## Examples, methods, and vignettes

There are three places to go after installation, depending on what you want to
work through:

- **The [blog series](/posts/2026-08-18-introducing-tidycreel.html)** follows
  small examples from [design objects](/posts/2026-08-27-design-object.html)
  and [sampling calendars](/posts/2026-09-03-sampling-calendar.html) through
  [roving interviews](/posts/2026-09-11-roving-interviews.html),
  [linked tables](/posts/2026-09-18-linked-tables.html),
  [effort](/posts/2026-09-25-effort-estimation.html),
  [catch, harvest, and release](/posts/2026-10-02-catch-harvest-release.html),
  and [diagnostics](/posts/2026-10-09-reading-diagnostics.html).
- **The companion book, [*Modern Creel Survey Analysis in R*](https://modern-creel-surveys.netlify.app/),**
  develops the reasoning behind those workflows: sampling design, estimands,
  uncertainty, and interpretation. It remains a work in progress as the methods,
  examples, and package develop.
- **The [full vignette collection](https://chrischizinski.com/tidycreel/articles/)**
  provides focused package walkthroughs. CRAN includes **24 vignettes**, covering
  getting started, survey designs, interview estimation, incomplete trips,
  effort and catch calculations, variance methods, scheduling, visualization,
  and more. They are also available directly from the
  [CRAN package page](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tidycreel/index.html).

To browse the installed vignettes or open the getting-started guide in R:

```r
browseVignettes("tidycreel")
vignette("tidycreel", package = "tidycreel")
```

The online collection is useful with a GitHub installation too, since that
installation does not build local vignettes by default. Recent blog examples
identify the 7.0.0 release they used; this announcement marks the 8.0.0 release.

If you try `tidycreel` with your own creel data, I would like to hear where the
data structures, diagnostics, or examples need more explanation. Questions are
welcome in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/chrischizinski/tidycreel/discussions),
and reproducible bug reports help through the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/chrischizinski/tidycreel/issues).
